newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Oct 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Oct 29.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Oct. 29:
WASHINGTON - Fairfax supervisors fired County Executive William Leidinger after his last-ditch bid to save his job failed to sway critics who concluded that after four years it was time for a change.
WASHINGTON - The Democratic National Committee will not file a preelection report detailing its contributions and spending for the first time in 22 years since the federal election law was written.
WASHINGTON - The image of a straight-shooting teller of truths is one of the few consistent elements in Bob Dole's scattershot campaign.
ALEXANDER CITY, Ala. - The Republican Party looks to the south to maintain its majority in the House of Representatives where open Democratic seats could help offset potential losses elsewhere.
ATLANTA - Richard Jewell, the man who went from hero to suspect to innocent in the Olympic Park bombing, described the past three months as a nightmare.
NEW YORK - Gisella Weisshaus, frustrated with the wall of silence, has become the first Holocaust survivor to sue a Swiss bank in the hopes of retrieving an abandoned account.

WASHINGTON - Haunted by the memory of being trapped in their homes during the Blizzard of 1996, residents are buying snow blowers at an astonishing rate and store officials say they can barely keep up with the demand.
